Subject: POC: Redwood Trial / Evaluation Plan & Success Criteria

Thanks again for the call today — great discussion, John & Priya. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC scoped and calendarized.

Recap of needs (from our discovery):
- Primary goal: reduce hallucinations and improve retrieval-quality for user-facing knowledge search (product KB + support articles).
- Target latency: 150-250ms p95 for single-turn generation in production.
- Throughput target during POC: support peak of ~5 req/s per model endpoint.
- Data & security: customer-managed S3 for logs, SOC2 evidence required for contract.

Proposed POC success criteria (please confirm / tweak):
1) Functional quality: improvement in top-1 relevance from current baseline (Acme system) by >= 10% (MRR metric on a representative eval set).
2) Latency: p95 <= 200ms for 95% of test traffic patterns.
3) Reliability: no more than 1 incident causing >5m downtime during the POC window.
4) Ops: ability to ingest streaming logs into your internal S3 and see token-level cost reports.

Evaluation plan (high level):
- Offline eval: we run an offline evaluation using your anonymized sample set (N=1,000 queries) with a rubric for relevance and hallucination labeling.
- Shadow/online: 2-week shadowing period where traffic is mirrored to Redwood and we capture live metrics (latency, throughput, qualitative flags).
- Grading rubric: each query gets a relevance score (0/1/2) and a hallucination flag; overall MRR computed and compared to baseline. Pass threshold = baseline + 10%.

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): align on success criteria & sign MAP.
- Week 1: share data sample and security questionnaire; infra setup (S3, VPC peering / access).
- Week 2-3: offline eval + tuning.
- Week 4-5: shadow mode with live traffic capture.
- Week 6: review results, executive summary, decision meeting.

Attachments: acme_poc_scope.pdf (draft scope), redwood_trial_checklist.xlsx (infrastructure checklist).

Next steps / asks for you:
- Confirm the success criteria above (especially the MRR uplift target and latency).
- Confirm a target kickoff week (we're proposing week of Mar 2).
- Share a 1,000-sample anonymized test set and a point-of-contact for security questionnaire.

Happy to hop on a quick 30-min sync if you'd prefer to walk through the plan.

Hi John / team — quick technical follow-up on format and the evaluation methodology.

Sample format: please provide a CSV with columns: query_id, query_text, context_blob (optional), baseline_response (optional). Anonymize any PII. If you prefer, we can provide a small example CSV template.

Offline eval plan (detailed):
- Dataset: N=1,000 queries sampled from production logs; we recommend stratified sampling across least-recent, most-frequent, and edge-case queries (approx 60/30/10 split).
- Labeling rubric: relevance score 0 (irrelevant), 1 (partial), 2 (highly relevant). Hallucination flag: 0/1. Two-labeler agreement required; any disagreement gets tie-break adjudicator.
- Metrics computed: MRR, Precision@1, Hallucination rate. Baseline run vs Redwood model variant(s).
- Success threshold: MRR >= baseline * 1.10 AND hallucination_rate <= 2% (or <= baseline if baseline <2%).
- Sign-off: Acme product + Redwood SE must agree on the auditable labeling sample (we usually provide a Google Sheet with label rows).

Online shadow plan (detailed):
- Duration: 2 weeks of mirrored traffic at 100% read-only (no user-facing responses).
- Capture: latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), token counts, model outputs for sampled queries, and flags for hallucination candidates.
- Safety: redact PII in transit and store only in your S3 bucket per agreement; we will not retain raw content beyond the POC retention period unless agreed.

Grade rubric proposal:
- For each sample batch: compute MRR_delta = MRR_redwood - MRR_baseline.
- Pass if MRR_delta >= +10% AND hallucination_rate <= 2%.
- Partial pass if MRR_delta between +5% and +10% with plan to address hallucination regressions documented.
- Fail otherwise; recommend retrospective tuning & another shadow run.

Owners (from Redwood):
- SE lead (evals): David Kim — infra, scripts, and labeling coordination.
- CS/engagement: Neha Kapoor — rollout, weekly checkpoints, exec summary.
